name: fastme
desc: Accurate and fast distance-based phylogeny inference program
why: Infers phylogenetic trees from distance matrices, real evolutionary biology you can run on your own data.

brief.what_it_is: FastME is a software package that infers phylogenetic trees from distance matrices. It takes a square PHYLIP distance matrix, or DNA, protein, or PHYLIP alignments from which it estimates distances, and outputs a tree. It implements Balanced Minimum Evolution (BME), a distance criterion closely related to Neighbor Joining, and refines the tree with NNI and SPR rearrangements. The homepage also hosts a web submission form for running analyses online.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the goal of the BME framework is to identify the phylogenetic tree that minimizes the total estimated evolutionary distance among taxa, and that FastME is aimed at accurate, fast reconstruction on large datasets where likelihood-based approaches may be computationally demanding.
brief.how_it_works: After building an initial tree, FastME refines the topology with rearrangement operations, Nearest Neighbor Interchange (NNI) and Subtree Pruning and Regrafting (SPR), to find trees with shorter total branch lengths at a computational cost comparable to NJ. It accepts DNA sequences, protein sequences, or precomputed distance matrices and offers several distance estimation methods. Bootstrap support and parallel computation are also listed.

commands_seen.context: Quoted from the web form's BioNJ pipeline description: the BioNJ mode preserves PHYLIP distance options and runs FastME with these flags and no refinement, with bootstrap consensus made by PHYLIP Consense.

brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install was on the homepage. The homepage has a Download link and a User guide link, but I did not follow them. The online service accepts PHYLIP alignments or square PHYLIP distance matrices, 1 to 100 data sets, and a Newick starting topology is optional.
brief.standout: It is a distance-based method that starts from an NJ-like tree and then searches for a better BME tree with SPR moves, aiming for likelihood-like accuracy at distance-method speed. The package is also published with a web front end that exposes model choices and bootstrapping.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows the 2015 MBE paper (FastME 2.0, Lefort, Desper, Gascuel) and a live execution API check, but gives no release date, last commit, or version.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage, which is a web page rather than a repository README, so I have no install instructions, licence, or platform details. The web service page notes that submitting an analysis is subject to Terms of Use. The homepage text does not state a licence.
quotes: FastME is a software package for the fast and accurate inference of phylogenetic trees from distance matrices.
Compared to classical Neighbor Joining approaches, FastME improves tree accuracy through efficient topological optimization procedures.

Thanks to its combination of speed, scalability, and accuracy, FastME is widely used for phylogenetic reconstruction, particularly for large datasets where likelihood-based approaches may be computationally demanding.
